applies_why: The judge text marks the Matthew 1:20 point UNDERDETERMINED while acknowledging the sentence's own words state the source, so it treats the verse as open rather than letting both meanings stand.
quote: D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb; answered in [CR3] LINK 2.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. When one verse's words carry two meanings at once, both stand; the verse is not open.
room: the phrase 'carry two meanings at once, both stand; the verse is not open': I weighed (1) the judge's UNDERDETERMINED treats Matthew 1:20 as open between source and covenant-origin, which the rule forbids; (2) it is merely weighing separately footed support, which the rule does not forbid.
why: The judge text labels the point UNDERDETERMINED even while saying the sentence's own words state the source, so it leaves a verse with two meanings open instead of letting both stand as K-S2 requires.
